feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: Nepal's hesitance to accept foreign help for flood relief under scrutiny
entry.summary: A group of the country's private sector power producers says Nepali authorities lost crucial time in rescuing hundreds of people trapped in hydropower tunnels.

entry.title: U.S., Venezuela strike oil deal. And, the staggering hidden toll of U.S. heat deaths
entry.summary: The U.S. and Venezuela have entered into an oil deal. And, NPR spent two years tracking heat-related deaths and found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat more than the official counts show.

entry.title: Russia's jet-powered drones bring empty Kyiv supermarket shelves and rattle Ukrainians
entry.summary: Russian forces relentlessly battered Kyiv and cities in the region around the Ukrainian capital for a fifth straight day, leaving some supermarket shelves bare after repeated strikes on warehouses.

entry.title: Attacks flare between the U.S. and Iran after a monthlong pause
entry.summary: U.S. threats erupt into attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran retaliates against U.S. targets in the United Arab Emirates and Jordan in the first exchange of fire since July 29.

entry.title: Hit shows from Edinburgh's Fringe festival are coming to America. Here are our top picks
entry.summary: The annual "anything goes" performing arts festival featured more than 4,200 performances this year. These are the ones we're still talking about.

entry.title: The U.S.-Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know
entry.summary: The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.

entry.title: Rescuers search for the missing after deadly flood along Nepal-Tibet border
entry.summary: China and Nepal continue to grapple with the devastation left by catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border, as rescuers search for the missing and assess widespread destruction.

entry.title: U.N. worker shares what aid is needed as Nepal recovers from devastating flood
entry.summary: NPR's A Martínez asks the United Nations' resident coordinator in Nepal, Lila Pieters Yahia, what more is needed to aid flood victims there.

entry.title: What Argentina gets right about youth soccer — and what the U.S. gets wrong
entry.summary: Argentina has produced some of the world's greatest soccer players. Could its youth system offer lessons for the United States?

entry.title: Families of pilgrims likely caught in floods are desperate for news from Nepal
entry.summary: Four days after catastrophic floods wiped out villages along the Nepal-China border, thousands are still missing. Families look for answers but hear nothing.
